free_tier.stated: 5,000 credits a month, no card, 5 concurrent requests, monthly refresh with no rollover

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

retention.stated: credits refresh monthly; top-up credits roll over one period on paid plans

egress.terms: not applicable: Markdown, HTML or JSON answers

interface_detail: REST fetch, extract and batch; crawl is a job plus a poll
chaining: The fetch-relay lane in the platform's read ladder; 1 credit plain makes it cheaper than ScrapingAnt for a page that needs no render

limits.value: a standard page is 1 credit, with JavaScript rendering 5, premium proxies 10, both 25
5 concurrent on Free, 20 on Build at USD 19 a month for 45K credits on monthly billing, USD 16 annual
one credit is one plain page, so the effective page cap is the credit count divided by 1, 5, 10 or 25

limits_note: the credit multiplier is the binding constraint: a plan quoted in credits buys a fifth to a twenty-fifth of its headline in pages, and the multiplier is what decides a plan

identity_cost.detail: no card, stated on the Free plan

evidence.proved: Free USD 0 with 5,000 credits a month and no card; standard page 1 credit, JavaScript rendering 5, premium proxies 10, both 25; Build 45,000 to 120,000 credits a month at USD 16 to 33 annual monthly and USD 19 to 39 monthly; Launch 250,000 to 700,000 at USD 58 to 108 annual monthly and USD 69 to 129 monthly; the page states that its headline price is the annual monthly rate, ten months paid for twelve

notes: The credit multiplier is the whole story: 5,000 plain pages, 1,000 rendered, 500 behind a premium proxy, 200 with both. Extract is free on top of the fetch it uses. Every per-1,000 figure in the paid lane uses the monthly-billing price, USD 69 for Launch and USD 19 for Build; quoting the annual rate as the price is 20% low.
